analysis:
Both changed files are Swift test code only (SandboxSetupTests.swift, SandboxTestSupport.swift). They add test coverage for the sandbox setup flow: a plan-mode installer (`--plan --json-progress`), background/waitlist approval events, fake installer scripts, and fixtures. No production source is changed in the supplied units, so no regression to the TB-013/T-061 installer-trust boundary, TB-012 hold socket, or A-019 can be shown from this evidence.

The fake installer scripts run only inside CLICommandSandbox with a stubbed CoordinatorStub, a `.invalid` server host and a temporary DARKBLOOM_SANDBOX_ROOT. They make no real network calls and use no real credentials. Fixture values (host UUID, user code WDJB-MJHT, team ID SLDQ2GJ6TL) are synthetic or public and are not secrets.

The tests assert the intended behavior that the plan step receives no `--yes` (SandboxSetupTests head lines ~125-130, 556) and that nothing is installed when the plan says no job fits (lines 562-591) or the host is ineligible (lines 753-779). They also assert that confirmation is required, or `--yes` passed, before installing (lines 803-831). These support T-061's owner-confirmation posture. One download serves both plan and install (the stub saw a single request, line 559).

A remaining question for integration: the production implementation of SandboxInstaller.planOption, planArguments, supportsPlan and SandboxSetupFlow is not in this batch. Whether the plan-mode run executes the downloaded script with the same staging, owner-only permissions and environment controls as the install run, and whether the plan run could do side effects before confirmation, depends on that code. The tests only show that a conforming fake installer installs nothing in plan mode. A malicious installer is already within T-061's accepted scope, since the script runs as the owner either way. The extra pre-confirmation execution of downloaded code in plan mode is worth a check against the production source, but it is not provable here.
